quiz.q: According to Sardar Patel's realist school of thought, what was the primary nature of the Chinese state and how should India respond?
options: China is an irredentist state, requiring India to maintain military preparedness rather than relying on appeasement.
China seeks civilisational harmony, requiring India to promote border trade and cultural exchanges.
China is economically interdependent, requiring India to adopt a pragmatic policy of engagement and containment.
China is a status-quo power, requiring India to sign bilateral treaties recognizing regional suzerainty.
quiz.why: Sardar Patel viewed China as an irredentist, land-grabbing state with offensive designs, arguing that the only way to avoid war was through continuous military preparedness.

quiz.q: Why did Nehru's 1954 Panchsheel Agreement face strong domestic criticism regarding India's strategic interests?
options: It demarcated the Line of Actual Control along the McDonald Line against military advice.
It formally recognized Chinese sovereignty over Tibet without securing any concrete reciprocal concessions for India.
It permitted China to build an all-weather highway across Aksai Chin without diplomatic protest.
It surrendered Indian claims over Arunachal Pradesh in exchange for trading rights at Nathu La.
quiz.why: Nehru was criticized in parliament because India accepted Tibet as Chinese territory and gave up traditional rights without gaining any concrete border settlement in return.

quiz.q: According to the notes, why is China reluctant to conclude the final phase of the three-phase border resolution process?
options: It insists on renegotiating the initial guiding principles established by the special representatives in 2003.
It refuses to conduct technical ground work until India joins its trans-regional infrastructure projects.
It fears a settlement would give India a free hand in Tibet and prefers settling from strength.
It demands that India withdraw all military checkposts from the middle sector before exchanging maps.
quiz.why: China worries that resolving the border dispute would allow India to create disturbances in Tibet, and prefers delaying settlement until the bilateral power gap widens further.

quiz.q: What structural factor primarily drives India's widening bilateral trade deficit with China?
options: India imports high-value agricultural produce while facing strict non-tariff barriers on manufactured consumer goods.
India bears steep licensing fees for sharing daily hydrological data on the Brahmaputra River system.
India faces high tariff rates exclusively applied to its raw material shipments entering Chinese ports.
India exports raw materials while importing manufactured items, facing closed sectors in pharmaceuticals and IT.
quiz.why: India's trade deficit stems from exporting low-value raw materials while importing manufactured goods, compounded by Chinese market restrictions on competitive Indian sectors like IT and pharmaceuticals.
